title: GTA 6 Guides Hub – How To Do Everything In Grand Theft Auto 6
summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and with Rockstar's massive open-world adventure now in your hands, there's going to be a lot to discover across Vice City and the wider state of Leonida. Whether you're looking for help with certain mechanics, side activities, money-making, or simply figuring out what to do next, our GTA 6 guides hub has you covered.

The game launched initially for Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5, with a PC release expected to follow, potentially in 2027. The game sees protagonists Jason and Lucia at the center of a story across Leonida. GameSpot's Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub will be updated regularly with new tips, secrets, walkthroughs, and other useful information as we learn more about the game.

The Buckingham Maverick is a great early-game pick if you just want to explore and reveal more of the map. Military helicopters in GTA 6

While you’re in the area, you might be interested in getting a military helicopter in GTA 6. There are several options like the machine-gunning Buzzard, sleek Valkyrie, and beefy Cargobob. All of these are in the Mile Zero Base just a short distance away from Southwind.

You must be careful, though, because this is a military base that’s on high alert. If you get spotted within its boundaries, you’ll be warned by police and soldiers. Dawdle for too long and you’ll be reported for committing a crime, earning an instant 4-star Wanted Level for good measure. Having countless troops, including those in armored vehicles, shooting at you is not a good way to start the day.

Amphibious helicopters

It’s also a good idea to find amphibious helicopters like the Nagasaki Sea Sparrow. One is near the speedway in the southwestern part of Hamlet, and the other is further west at the halfway point between the town and Watson Bay. As the term implies, these types of choppers can take off/land on water, making them integral for thorough exploration of the seas surrounding Leonida.

There are many helicopters flying all over Vice City, and you can grab one of them by searching for the helipad icons on your map. Buildings with helipads on the roof tend to have interiors that you can enter, as well as elevators that can take you to the top floor. From there, you just need to hijack the vehicle and zip away to safety.

title: How To Steal And Register Cars With Advanced Trackers In GTA 6
summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has a massive world, and you can be sure that there are thousands of vehicles driving across the countryside at any given point in time. While the vast majority can be hijacked without worries--well, aside from cops that might see you--a select few have anti-theft devices that make them an unbearable hassle. Thankfully, there are ways to steal vehicles with Advanced Trackers.

Advanced Trackers: How exactly do they work?

The Advanced Trackers in GTA 6 can be seen if you scan most high-end vehicles like sports cars and luxury cars. Basically, if it looks expensive and sells for a high price, you can bet that it has an Advanced Tracker. Here’s how the device works:

  • Stolen vehicles with a Standard Tracker ping their location only if (a) they’ve significantly slowed down or stopped, and (b) a police car is nearby.
  • Advanced Trackers, meanwhile, ping their location if you go below a certain speed. You essentially need to put your pedal to the metal when driving them. Otherwise, the police would know your exact location.

Given the risk, most fence NPCs in the game won’t even accept stolen vehicles with Advanced Trackers. Well, except for one fella: Randy.

The legit method: Do missions for Randy

Randy is the one NPC in the game that accepts stolen cars with Advanced Trackers, but there are some caveats:

  • You meet Randy while tackling main missions in chapter 3. He’ll give you a task to steal a Zorrusso, which also nets you the Key Cloner, a tool that allows you to hijack keyless cars.
  • At this point, Randy and various Pay ‘n’ Spray shops will start accepting stolen vehicles with Standard Trackers.
  • He’ll also tell you that he has a “wishlist” of sorts: A dozen or so high-end cars that you need to boost and bring to his garage.
  • Note that some targets do have Advanced Trackers. He’ll only accept these as long as they’re part of his wishlist. Since he’ll keep them, you won’t be able to own/register them at all.
  • Again, you need to drive fast to prevent the tracker from triggering. But you also have to be careful since the sell value of the car will decrease depending on the damage.

Now, let’s say you’ve completed all of Randy’s requests. Come chapter 4, Randy will give you one more mission. This time, you need to boost a Mamba GT.

After that ordeal, you’ll be able to remove Advanced Trackers via Pay ‘n’ Spray shops in Leonida. Yes, you’ll finally be able to register/own all those high-end vehicles you keep seeing in Vice City.

The exploit method: Have your partner drive it

There’s also another method if you wish to steal cars with Advanced Trackers in GTA 6. It’s an exploit that involves fiddling around with partner controls. Here’s how to do it:

  • Have your partner tag along while you’re exploring.
  • Locate a car with an Advanced Tracker. Don’t do anything with it yet.
  • Look for a car near it, one that only has a Standard Tracker or no tracker at all. Make sure you unlock that vehicle.
  • Next, unlock the door of the car with the Advanced Tracker… and immediately exit it.
  • Open the partner interface by holding L2/LT. Then, select “You Drive.” This will cause your partner to enter the last vehicle that you interacted with--i.e. the one with the Advanced Tracker.
  • As for your own character, simply hop on to the other car that you jacked. Then, open the partner interface again and select “Follow.” (If your partner is driving the vehicle, they won’t trigger the tracker’s system.)
  • Drive your lowly vehicle to Randy’s shop, and watch as your partner follows behind you at a leisurely pace.
  • When you’re in front of Randy’s garage, simply switch to your partner and deliver the vehicle.

That’s it. No police chases, no need to drive over the speed limit, and no panicking due to the tracker’s alarm potentially going off.

Tenebrae Lux and the JoySystem console

Tenebrae Lux is a “video game within a video game.” You can play it once you have access to the JoySystem console, which occurs during a main mission called Feng Shui.

In the GTA 6 Tenebrae Lux game, you play as someone simply known as “The Man.” You find yourself stranded on an island, and your goal is to solve puzzles to reach the lighthouse at the top of the hill. What makes the whole experience memorable is that the game is purely in black and white, and its atmosphere is further enhanced by eerie sound effects, disturbing visuals, and randomized clues/content.

Tenebrae Lux Sliding Block Puzzles

When you first start Tenebrae Lux, you’ll see the lighthouse in the distance. To your left, you’ll spot a fishing wharf and a couple of rundown shacks. At this point, you need to interact with the game boards in the area to do the Sliding Block Puzzles. There are two in the wharf and one in the small shack just beside it.

Here’s what the Sliding Block Puzzle mechanics entail:

  • There are three types of pieces on the board: pyramids, square plates, and stacked blocks. Your goal is to clear out/destroy everything.
  • The pyramids can be moved horizontally or vertically until they hit the board edge or another object. They remain intact after destroying adjacent square plates, but they’re expended if they destroy a block.
  • Stacked blocks can also be moved and they destroy adjacent pyramids. However, they have no effect on square plates. You mostly just move them to create a path so your pyramids don’t end up adjacent to them unless absolutely necessary.
  • Square plates cannot be moved at all.

A bit of trial and error is necessary, and you can reset by exiting the board interface. Likewise, the types of pieces and their placement on each board tends to be randomized per playthrough, so there’s no clear-cut solution for everything.

Note 1: Once you’ve completed the three required Sliding Block Puzzles, you’re free to enter the bunker.

Note 2: Don’t forget to pick up the document next to one of the puzzle boards in the wharf. There are 11 documents in total, and not everything can be discovered in a single playthrough.

Additional puzzles and collectible documents - Part 1

You’ll realize that there are a some some strange occurrences in your surroundings:

  • The haunted shack atop the sloping path has its front door locked. However, if you check the porch at the back, you’ll see an optional Sliding Block Puzzle. Solve it to enter the shack so you can pick up a document.
  • If you follow the coastal path, you’ll stumble upon a mysterious door at the edge of a pier. It’s the “Door That Leads to Nowhere.”
  • Just beyond that, there’s another optional Sliding Block Puzzle. It unlocks the cargo container, which has one more document.

Tenebrae Lux Bunker Phone Puzzle

Once you’re ready, go through the well-lit door opposite the wharf. It leads you to the GTA 6 Tenebrae Lux Bunker Phone Puzzle, which is, in our opinion, one helluva doozy.

Upon entering the main room in the bunker, you’ll see all sorts of gizmos and contraptions. Now, you have to keep your eyes peeled for clues related to anomalies.

Note: We encourage you to enable subtitles and closed captions so you don’t miss out on voiceover hints.

Randomized dates

Each time you enter the bunker room, that particular instance can be one of six potential dates: October 11, October 14, October 20, October 23, October 27, or October 30. You can find out what day it is by inspecting the calendar on the wall. Your character will either make an off-handed remark about it or you’ll see dates that have been crossed out.

It’s important that you know what day it is for that particular instance since you need to figure out a specific anomaly. This mechanic is also tied to the solution for the puzzle.

Room anomalies

There are several objects that you need to check in the room. We’ve listed them based on how early you’ll see or hear them upon entering:

  • Zuchworks Engine Greek letter - The moment you enter the room, you might see this notification: “Developed using Zuchworks Engine.” This might have a Greek alphabet--i.e. alpha, beta, gamma, and so on.
  • Telephone rings - Upon entering the room, the phone might ring. Count how many times it rings.
  • Music - Upon entering the room, you’ll hear music (like an old-timey shanty of sorts). Listen closely to the speed of the music and any distortion.
  • Painting of Roman-style pillars - On the shelf to your right. Look at the pillars to see if they form a Roman numeral.
  • Tape recorder - On the desk to your right. See if it can be played and listen to the date.
  • Classified document - On the desk to your right. Check if the Cascade File Number is written down or redacted.
  • Photo - On the desk to your right. Count how many people are in the photograph.
  • Vinyl record - On the metal barrels at the left-hand side of the room. Check the price of The Bateson Brothers record.
  • Desk lamp and morse code - The lamp that you need to check is to the left of the calendar. A document about morse code might appear on the console terminal.
  • Clock - Above the console terminal. Look at the time.

Note: Keep in mind that not all of these objects will appear in your playthrough. For instance, you might not see a painting on the shelf or you might not be able to interact with the document or tape recorder. That’s totally fine. There will always be six important objects among the options listed above.

What to do in succeeding rooms

Okay, you’ve checked the date on the calendar and you’ve also inspected the six objects in the initial room. Don’t forget to take a screenshot of each of them or jot down the details in your Notes app.

Then, go through the door to the right of the phone and head up the steps. Surprise! You’re back in the same room… but there’s something fishy going on.

  • Go ahead and investigate the calendar to learn about the current date for that particular instance--i.e. the second room.
  • Then, inspect the six objects in the room once more. Be on the lookout for any changes that are out of the ordinary. Examples include the clock showing a different time, the vinyl record having a different price, or the desk lamp suddenly flickering on and off.

title: GTA 6 Has Massive Underground Caves Worth Diving Into
summary:
Take a break from all the car chases and crimes in Grand Theft Auto 6, and relax in the quaint Emerald Springs resort. Oh, what's that? Is there something interesting nearby? Yes, it looks like a tourist attraction, the Selkie Hole, is worth a look. Perhaps there are hidden rewards that await you in the depths of the underwater cave.

    • The blue pools

    • Potential for more secrets: The Hollow Earth theory

Where to find the Selkie Hole in Grand Theft Auto 6

The Selkie Hole in GTA 6 can be found in Kelly County. Specifically, it’s in a large nature reserve known as Emerald Springs. To get there, follow the road leading southeast out of Port Gellhorn or west from Hamlet.

The blue pools

Upon arriving, be sure to check the nearby scannables using your WAiNK app. Then, make your way to the western part of the park as shown on the map above. You’ll find a visually striking place, a pool with crystal clear blue water.

From there, look for a small shed that has the Selkie Hole signage. This leads to the diving area, which also has Scuba Gear for you and your partner to equip. Likewise, note that the cave entrance here counts as a WAiNK Curiosity when scanned.

Cave diving for rewards and following the ropes

From the diving area, keep to the left as you go underwater. You’ll see a ropeline with arrows. The arrows actually point toward the exit which, in this case, is the diving area itself.

So, for now, follow the rope as it leads in the opposite direction. Along the way, you’ll be able to pick up a couple of meteorites and the Explorer’s Knife legendary weapon. You’ll end up at the other end of the tunnel--i.e. the pool with clear blue water.

Note: Pay attention to the remaining oxygen in your oxygen tank. You have to return to the diving area if you want to refill it or equip your Scuba Gear again.

More tunnels and meteorites

title: The Fastest Cars In GTA 6 And How To Get Them
summary:
The state of Leonida is home to some of the rarest and most expensive cars we've ever seen in the Grand Theft Auto franchise. GTA 6 features over a dozen supercars, which are always the pinnacle of the vehicle food chain. While you'll likely take any supercar during the early or mid-game, you'll eventually want to drive the fastest car in GTA 6.

Driving the fastest car in Leonida will require you to acquire a legendary vehicle or wait until your character can afford one later on in the story. With GTA 6's new car-stealing restrictions, you can't just take a supercar off the streets and make it your own. However you decide to get a supercar, you'll still want to know which ones go the fastest.

Fastest cars in GTA 6

Technically, the fastest overall cars in GTA 6 will depend on what custom mods you have installed on certain cars. For example, you can bring a car's max speed to 9.0 or higher (out of 10) by upgrading its engine, transmission, and more, but that's not the car's default speed.

For this list, we'll just be covering which cars are the fastest by default in GTA 6. This means looking at the car's stock speed when it has no additional upgrades installed. This list is also just cars, as we'll go over the fastest overall vehicles, including motorcycles, planes, and bikes, in a future list.

Here are the top five fastest cars we've come across in GTA 6, ranked by their top speeds:

5. Pfister Comet S2

Coming in as the fifth-fastest car in GTA 6 is the Pfister Comet S2, a slight surprise since this vehicle isn't classified as a supercar. However, it's plenty fast, with a stock speed rating of 7.7, beating out some truly impressive supercars that look like they would be faster. Without spoiling anything from the story, the Comet S2 is an option you could acquire later on in GTA 6.

4. Piccia Furia

You knew some Italian muscle was going to be on this list, and the Piccia Furia comes in as the fourth-fastest car in GTA 6. Featuring a stock speed rating of 7.8, the Furia is a fairly rare car in Leonida, as you don't often see it parked at the luxurious NINE1NINE strip club or along the streets of the Vice City beaches.

3. Pegassi Vitello

Pegassi has long been one of the best car brands in the GTA franchise, so it's no surprise to see it on this list. In GTA 6, the Pegassi Vitello is the third-fastest car in the game, with a stock speed rating of 8.2. There's a significant gap between the Vitello and the two slower cars on this list in terms of speed, acceleration, and handling.

2. Progen Emerus

GTA Online players will immediately recognize the Progen Emerus, and it's made a return in GTA 6. When it's fully maxed out with upgrades and mods, the Emerus can reach a speed rating of 9.0 and above. However, even with all of its stock parts, you'll have a speed rating of 8.3 with the Progren Emerus.

1. Truffade Thrax

Topping the list of the fastest cars in GTA 6 is the Truffade Thrax. This supercar is significantly faster than anything else we've found so far in Leonida, featuring a stock speed rating of 8.7. That's higher than most cars can reach with fully upgraded parts, so you're going to be flying with the Thrax if you can manage to fully upgrade it. To guarantee getting one, read our guide on the NoFlusher tag locations.

For some honorable mentions, we have the Pegassi Tempesta (7.6 speed rating) and the Granforma Zorrusso (7.5 speed rating). New cars that haven't been discovered yet in GTA 6 could change this list in the future, but these are the fastest cars known to be in the game right now.

For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: Xbox Game Pass Kicks Off December With Horror, Cozy Adventures, And More
summary:
One last month of 2026 brings two more waves of Xbox Game Pass titles to close out the year. Subscribers can once again look forward to some new arrivals in the Xbox Game Pass library, ranging from gruesome co-op action to wholesome adventures featuring helpful mice on a mission. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so while this list isn’t complete yet, we do know what you can expect in the first half of December. As usual, we’ll update this page once Xbox reveals the full lineup for this first batch.

For now, you can look forward to an eclectic mix of games, starting with The Outlast Trials. Released in 2024, it’s a co-op survival-horror game that throws a team of up to four players into a gauntlet of deadly trials, where evasion is key to victory. You can also play it solo, and if the onslaught of festive season cheerfulness is getting to you, then this will be a nice–but brutal–change of pace.

If you’d prefer to focus on the coziness of the season, then Hela: Of Mice and Magic looks like a fun time. Set in a magical forest inspired by Scandinavian lands, the game follows a group of mice on a journey to help people, at the behest of an old witch who can’t make the trip herself. This is also a day-one release for Xbox Game Pass, and it’ll be joined by World of Tanks Blitz on the same day. On December 3, Freestyle Football 2 launches, bringing fast-paced, 5v5 multiplayer street soccer to Xbox and PC, and on December 14, you can grab Nubby’s Number Factory, a roguelite game all about making big numbers.

Xbox Game Pass December Wave 1 Games

December 1

  • The Outlast Trials (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) — Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Hela: Of Mice and Magic (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) — Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass
  • World of Tanks Blitz

December 3

  • Freestyle Football 2

December 14

  • Nubby’s Number Factory

If you missed it, November brought a solid selection of releases. The first wave added the dungeon-crawling roguelike deck-building game Dungeon Crawlers to more Game Pass tiers, along with Warhammer Survivors and John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando. The Game Pass library expanded further later in November, with some Paw Patrol fun for the kiddos, High on Life 2, and the pretty good long-distance stealth game Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2.

title: All NoFlusher Tags In GTA 6
summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has several moments that rely heavily on over-the-top silliness. One, in particular, involves poo. Specifically, it’s about a group of individuals who do not want people to waste their, uh, waste, for fear of cloning and other sinister machinations. So, when you’re ready, it’s time to meet the gang and collect the NoFlusher Tags.

The NoFlusher narrative arcs in Grand Theft Auto 6

If you’ve been gathering collectibles all over Leonida, you’ve likely chanced upon a strange WAiNK Curiosity, that of a NoFlushers Homestead. One pamphlet that’s been left behind even coerces citizens to avoid flushing their feces down the toilet. Instead, folks are encouraged to turn poop into odd by-products like pottery, soap, and even organic food. It’s downright disgusting, but it’s guaranteed to make you chuckle, too.

Now, assuming you’ve made your way to Vice City, you’ll be given the opportunity to join the group proper:

  • First, you need to use the WAiNK app on your phone to scan the “Stop! Don’t Flush! #NoFlushers” QR code. You can find this poster/QR code in public bathrooms, like the one in Dynamix Gym just north of your safehouse in chapter 3.
  • Once you’ve done that, someone will tell you to meet up at Frank’s Waffles, and you’ll be able to mark the location on your map. This leads to a mission called The Final Flush.
  • At the same time, you can stumble upon a mystery where you look for NoFlusher Tags in GTA 6. Your goal here is to look for utility markings/scribbles on pavements and roads.

NoFlusher tag locations

The GTA 6 NoFlusher Tags appear as light blue scribbles with a toilet symbol drawn for good measure. The moment you scan your first one, you’ll get invited to a group chat by none other than Cal.

Several members with aliases then welcome you to the group, and you learn that they’re on the lookout for someone named Andrew Node. It seems that Node has been extracting everyone’s excrement to create a clone army using DNA.

You’re then tasked by the other members to scan utility markings with your WAiNK app. There are a total of 15 NoFlusher Tags in Vice City, though you only need to scan 10 to progress to the next stage of the mission.

NoFlusher Tag #1

Along the sidewalk on Koko Boulevard just past the bridge that leads to Ocean Beach.

NoFlusher Tag #2

Near the southern tip of Shore Drive right across from the Janus building.

NoFlusher Tag #3

Directly north of the second tag. It’s on the sidewalk across The Buckingham.

NoFlusher Tag #4

Continue north along Shore Drive until you’re slightly past Muscle Sands. Then, look to your left and check the area in front of the Daiquiri Bar.

NoFlusher Tag #5

From Shore Drive, go west to the Rococo Rich jewelry store, which should have its own icon on the map.

NoFlusher Tag #6

At the junction of Huevo Street, off to the side of the Bean Machine coffee shop.

NoFlusher Tag #7

Head to Portside Lane in the western portion of Ocean Beach. You’ll see this GTA 6 NoFlusher Tag along the bend on the road.

NoFlusher Tag #8

Keep going north from where you got NoFlushers Tag #7. Eventually, you’ll reach Harborside Avenue. The scribbles are on the sidewalk just before the tiny roundabout.

NoFlusher Tag #9

This is on Cabega Street just southeast of the above scannable object. It’s outside a Tootsie Katz - All You Can Eat Shrimp restaurant.

NoFlusher Tag #10

Found along D Street. It’s outside a Fuji Kitchen with a “free ramen on your birthday” promotion. The Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank is also nearby.

NoFlusher Tag #11

Found on Barlow Street. The drawing is in front of the cafe and restroom sheds.

NoFlusher Tag #12

Scan this marking along Oleander Boulevard on Oldby Island. It’s by the side of the road that leads to the bridge.

NoFlusher Tag #13

Found on the sidewalk outside the Hide Tide Hotel and Restaurant.

NoFlusher Tag #14

In front of a large residential complex’s fountain on Northside Avenue.

NoFlusher Tag #15

Keep heading north-northeast and scan this drawing along Mariposa Avenue.

Where to find CantCloneThis89’s hideout

After you scan at least 10 NoFlusher Tags, people in the group will start to panic, saying that Node knows their intentions. As your buddies leave the chat, you receive a DM from the moderator--CantCloneThis89--saying that you should meet him in his hideout. It’s marked on your map, so just head there when you’re able to.

Upon arriving at the storage unit, read the note and flip it. At the back, you’ll see the code 8-5-5-4-0-1-3. Interact with the keypad and input the code to open the unit. Inside, you’ll see how far gone CantCloneThis89 seems to be. In any case, check the boards to glean more clues:

  • The map has an island in the middle encircled.
  • Open the laptop and read the info about Andrew Node’s address. He lives in Sabal Circle, Starfish Island. (It’s the second house on the right.)
  • Some messages in the laptop imply that CantCloneThis89 doesn’t know if he’s still a real person or if he’s been cloned.

Andrew Node’s home and NoFlusher Tags reward: The Truffade Thrax

You might think that it’s a good idea to drive to Starfish Island. Well, no, that simply won’t do. It’s a gated community, and the guards will warn you to leave. If you keep pestering them, they might fight back or call the cops.

Here are our suggestions:

  • Open the map and click on the house’s location on Starfish Island. Then, call a RydeMe so you can fast travel there.
  • When you get out, one security guard will accost you. Eliminate him silently to avoid alerting others.
  • Next, bring down the two guards inside the yard.

Once the coast is clear, open the garage door to receive an awesome prize. It’s none other than a Truffade Thrax. This vehicle, which looks like a Bugatti Chiron, happens to be one of the fastest cars in the entire game.

Registering this vehicle is very costly, as it requires $70,000 cash. If you don’t have a lot to spare, you can leave it in a garage or in the two parking spaces in your safehouse. That way, it won’t disappear forever.

How To Complete The Final Flush

The Final Flush mission takes you on a quick romp to learn about Andrew Node’s plots… and where all the poop seems to be going. Remember that fella who contacted you after you scanned the QR code? Well, you might want to visit Frank’s Waffles, so go ahead and track the mission on your map.

Meet Dr. Merle and follow his directions

The Final Flush in GTA 6 introduces you to Dr. Merle, another conspiracy theorist and NoFlushers member who seeks to learn more about Andrew Node’s fiendishly fecal plans. When you chat with him in the restaurant, he’ll tell you that he swallowed a tracker, which he’ll flush down the toilet.

This leads to a sequence where you need to drive Dr. Merle around Vice City. The waypoint disappears intermittently, but Dr. Merle gives you instructions--i.e. Go south, go east, go straight, and the like. Whatever he says, make sure you look at the orientation of your minimap so that you’re going in the right direction.

The sewage treatment plant

Eventually, the waypoint will appear, and it will guide you to the sewage treatment plant. Merle remarks that this is how Node collects DNA specimens. All the waste materials that get flushed end up in the plant.

  • Merle will attempt to lockpick the gate and a security guard in a vehicle will approach. You can try to defuse the situation, though it’s possible to miss the prompt if Merle is still speaking. (We were unable to respond during our playthrough, but that was fine since the guard still went on his merry way.)
  • In the generator room, wait for Merle to say that the tracker is directly below you. Then, go upstairs and interact with the control panel.
  • Click the second and third buttons on the left, then press the button in the middle. This will reveal a hidden passageway to the cloning vat.

What should you do with Dr. Merle?

Dr. Merle is aghast upon seeing what he believes to be a cloning vat, and he feels that it’s his responsibility to see where it leads. He goes inside the vat, which slowly fills with icky water. He’ll tell you that you need to press the button to flush him (wherever that may lead).

Here’s what happens depending on your decision regarding Dr. Merle in GTA 6:

  • If you decide to ignore Merle’s order, he’ll drown due to the water in the vat.
  • If you decide to flush Merle, he’ll disappear and the vat will be empty.

Around this time, the guards will have caught wind of you, and they’ll call the police soon enough:

  • If you wait in the room, you still have to fight the guards and the cops, before you make your escape.
  • If you go inside the cloning vat, it will fill with water and you’ll get flushed down, just like Dr. Merle.

Assuming you chose the latter, you’ll receive a permanent stamina boost for your characters. This concludes these two quests about the NoFlushers in GTA 6. However, something more unnerving awaits later. If you sail to Frampton Island north of Lummox County, you’ll discover a hidden bunker. Input this code--3-6-1-2--and check what’s inside.

You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

  • First, you need to use the WAiNK app on your phone to scan the “Stop! Don’t Flush! #NoFlushers” QR code. You can find this poster/QR code in public bathrooms, like the one in Dynamix Gym just north of your safehouse in chapter 3.
  • Once you’ve done that, someone will tell you to meet up at Frank’s Waffles, and you’ll be able to mark the location on your map. This leads to a mission called The Final Flush.
  • At the same time, you can stumble upon a mystery where you look for NoFlusher Tags in GTA 6. Your goal here is to look for utility markings/scribbles on pavements and roads.

NoFlusher tag locations

The GTA 6 NoFlusher Tags appear as light blue scribbles with a toilet symbol drawn for good measure. The moment you scan your first one, you’ll get invited to a group chat by none other than Cal.

Several members with aliases then welcome you to the group, and you learn that they’re on the lookout for someone named Andrew Node. It seems that Node has been extracting everyone’s excrement to create a clone army using DNA.

You’re then tasked by the other members to scan utility markings with your WAiNK app. There are a total of 15 NoFlusher Tags in Vice City, though you only need to scan 10 to progress to the next stage of the mission.

NoFlusher Tag #1

Along the sidewalk on Koko Boulevard just past the bridge that leads to Ocean Beach.

NoFlusher Tag #2

Near the southern tip of Shore Drive right across from the Janus building.

NoFlusher Tag #3

Directly north of the second tag. It’s on the sidewalk across The Buckingham.

NoFlusher Tag #4

Continue north along Shore Drive until you’re slightly past Muscle Sands. Then, look to your left and check the area in front of the Daiquiri Bar.

NoFlusher Tag #5

From Shore Drive, go west to the Rococo Rich jewelry store, which should have its own icon on the map.

NoFlusher Tag #6

At the junction of Huevo Street, off to the side of the Bean Machine coffee shop.

NoFlusher Tag #7

Head to Portside Lane in the western portion of Ocean Beach. You’ll see this GTA 6 NoFlusher Tag along the bend on the road.

NoFlusher Tag #8

Keep going north from where you got NoFlushers Tag #7. Eventually, you’ll reach Harborside Avenue. The scribbles are on the sidewalk just before the tiny roundabout.

NoFlusher Tag #9

This is on Cabega Street just southeast of the above scannable object. It’s outside a Tootsie Katz - All You Can Eat Shrimp restaurant.

NoFlusher Tag #10

Found along D Street. It’s outside a Fuji Kitchen with a “free ramen on your birthday” promotion. The Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank is also nearby.

NoFlusher Tag #11

Found on Barlow Street. The drawing is in front of the cafe and restroom sheds.

NoFlusher Tag #12

Scan this marking along Oleander Boulevard on Oldby Island. It’s by the side of the road that leads to the bridge.

NoFlusher Tag #13

Found on the sidewalk outside the Hide Tide Hotel and Restaurant.

NoFlusher Tag #14

In front of a large residential complex’s fountain on Northside Avenue.

NoFlusher Tag #15

Keep heading north-northeast and scan this drawing along Mariposa Avenue.

Where to find CantCloneThis89’s hideout

After you scan at least 10 NoFlusher Tags, people in the group will start to panic, saying that Node knows their intentions. As your buddies leave the chat, you receive a DM from the moderator--CantCloneThis89--saying that you should meet him in his hideout. It’s marked on your map, so just head there when you’re able to.

Upon arriving at the storage unit, read the note and flip it. At the back, you’ll see the code 8-5-5-4-0-1-3. Interact with the keypad and input the code to open the unit. Inside, you’ll see how far gone CantCloneThis89 seems to be. In any case, check the boards to glean more clues:

  • The map has an island in the middle encircled.
  • Open the laptop and read the info about Andrew Node’s address. He lives in Sabal Circle, Starfish Island. (It’s the second house on the right.)
  • Some messages in the laptop imply that CantCloneThis89 doesn’t know if he’s still a real person or if he’s been cloned.

Andrew Node’s home and NoFlusher Tags reward: The Truffade Thrax

You might think that it’s a good idea to drive to Starfish Island. Well, no, that simply won’t do. It’s a gated community, and the guards will warn you to leave. If you keep pestering them, they might fight back or call the cops.

Here are our suggestions:

  • Open the map and click on the house’s location on Starfish Island. Then, call a RydeMe so you can fast travel there.
  • When you get out, one security guard will accost you. Eliminate him silently to avoid alerting others.
  • Next, bring down the two guards inside the yard.

Once the coast is clear, open the garage door to receive an awesome prize. It’s none other than a Truffade Thrax. This vehicle, which looks like a Bugatti Chiron, happens to be one of the fastest cars in the entire game.

Registering this vehicle is very costly, as it requires $70,000 cash. If you don’t have a lot to spare, you can leave it in a garage or in the two parking spaces in your safehouse. That way, it won’t disappear forever.

How To Complete The Final Flush

The Final Flush mission takes you on a quick romp to learn about Andrew Node’s plots… and where all the poop seems to be going. Remember that fella who contacted you after you scanned the QR code? Well, you might want to visit Frank’s Waffles, so go ahead and track the mission on your map.

Meet Dr. Merle and follow his directions

The Final Flush in GTA 6 introduces you to Dr. Merle, another conspiracy theorist and NoFlushers member who seeks to learn more about Andrew Node’s fiendishly fecal plans. When you chat with him in the restaurant, he’ll tell you that he swallowed a tracker, which he’ll flush down the toilet.

This leads to a sequence where you need to drive Dr. Merle around Vice City. The waypoint disappears intermittently, but Dr. Merle gives you instructions--i.e. Go south, go east, go straight, and the like. Whatever he says, make sure you look at the orientation of your minimap so that you’re going in the right direction.

The sewage treatment plant

Eventually, the waypoint will appear, and it will guide you to the sewage treatment plant. Merle remarks that this is how Node collects DNA specimens. All the waste materials that get flushed end up in the plant.

  • Merle will attempt to lockpick the gate and a security guard in a vehicle will approach. You can try to defuse the situation, though it’s possible to miss the prompt if Merle is still speaking. (We were unable to respond during our playthrough, but that was fine since the guard still went on his merry way.)
  • In the generator room, wait for Merle to say that the tracker is directly below you. Then, go upstairs and interact with the control panel.
  • Click the second and third buttons on the left, then press the button in the middle. This will reveal a hidden passageway to the cloning vat.

What should you do with Dr. Merle?

Dr. Merle is aghast upon seeing what he believes to be a cloning vat, and he feels that it’s his responsibility to see where it leads. He goes inside the vat, which slowly fills with icky water. He’ll tell you that you need to press the button to flush him (wherever that may lead).

Here’s what happens depending on your decision regarding Dr. Merle in GTA 6:

  • If you decide to ignore Merle’s order, he’ll drown due to the water in the vat.
  • If you decide to flush Merle, he’ll disappear and the vat will be empty.

Around this time, the guards will have caught wind of you, and they’ll call the police soon enough:

  • If you wait in the room, you still have to fight the guards and the cops, before you make your escape.
  • If you go inside the cloning vat, it will fill with water and you’ll get flushed down, just like Dr. Merle.

Assuming you chose the latter, you’ll receive a permanent stamina boost for your characters. This concludes these two quests about the NoFlushers in GTA 6. However, something more unnerving awaits later. If you sail to Frampton Island north of Lummox County, you’ll discover a hidden bunker. Input this code--3-6-1-2--and check what’s inside.

You’re going to feel lost as you explore the cities, beachfronts, and seedy underbelly of Leonida. If you need more help navigating the massive game world and tackling its activities, be sure to check our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: Where To Find All 1010 Murals In GTA 6 To Get A Free Car And Garage
summary:
Around halfway through Grand Theft Auto 6’s campaign, you’ll reach Vice City. You’ll spend several hours just tackling missions and gathering collectibles. While you’re at it, we encourage you to look for the 1010 Murals as well. That’s because this activity is somewhat missable and the rewards--the ‘95 Grotti Cheetah and a free garage--are things you definitely want.

      • Mural #2: Extraction Service
      • Mural #3: Loophole Architecture

      • Mural #5: Privatized Pains Socialized Gains
    • 1010 Murals reward location

1010 Murals activity requirement and mechanics

The GTA 6 1010 Murals activity initially requires you to read a specific Snapmatic post from an artist named 1010. It tells of a collaboration/cross-promotion with the manufacturer Grotti.

Here’s the kicker: As far as we can tell, Snapmatic posts tend to disappear/get replaced as you advance through the campaign. Upon checking, it looks like 1010’s Snapmatic post remains active from the early to mid-point of chapter 3. This is roughly up to 55% story completion, so it’s just before you start the Cartel Heist arc.

Assuming you’ve read 1010’s post, here’s what you need to do next:

  • Go to specific locations that have 1010’s signature mark: a black and white orb that slightly resembles a meteor or an eyeball.
  • Stand on or next to those marks. Your controller should vibrate telling you that you’re on the correct spot.
  • Look for a fragmented mural in the vicinity.
  • Open the Camera app on your phone and take a picture of the formed mural (R2 or RT).

Map: 1010 Murals in Vice City

The map below shows the locations of the five murals that you must take photos of. We’ve also included an icon for the reward that you obtain much later.

Mural #1: Compliance Theater

Travel to Mariner’s Highway in Downtown and look for Piker Financial Services. Off to the side, there’s a door that you can unlock stealthily if you already have the Snap Gun. If not, you could kick it down, though that would trigger an alarm.

Likewise, there’s a worker in the next corridor, and they’ll warn you when you enter the building. Try to defuse the situation or incapacitate them without being seen by other NPCs.

From there, ride the elevator to the rooftop, then climb up the ladder all the way to the top of the tower. 1010’s symbol is on a board, so just stand near it and take a photo of the mural below.

Mural #2: Extraction Service

This 1010 Mural in GTA 6 is directly north of the one that we mentioned earlier. Go to Catalan Boulevard and look for the New Quay Plaza.  Head to the opposite side of the rooftop and look for the adjacent buildings with a mural. 

Mural #3: Loophole Architecture

The next artwork is in Rockridge, specifically in a tenement building on Northbrook Drive. If it’s your first time entering this apartment complex, you’ll also find out that it’s a gang hideout and robbery opportunity. In any case, head up the elevator when you can and take a photo of the stadium across the street.

Mural #4: You Signed the Terms and Conditions

Okay, we’re going out on a limb by saying that this particular 1010 Mural in GTA 6 might cause headaches. It’s located on NE 2nd Avenue, which is just southwest of your apartment in Vice City. Here’s the problem:

  • Once you arrive at the location, you’ll see 1010’s marker at street level. You’ll also notice the colorful tram station up ahead.
  • The idea is to wait for the tram with unique design/colors, and then take a picture of it once it briefly stops at that station.
  • The issue is that the specific train might take a while, which can be a hassle if you have to wait for too long.

Note: If possible, try to check if your controller would vibrate when a generic train passes. Perhaps a photo of that could still be added to your tally.

Mural #5: Privatized Pains Socialized Gains

This one is on Barlow Street and it’s near Effluvia, the high-end bar and restaurant where you meet Brian and Lori as part of a main mission. Stand near the mark and take a photo of the stadium just across from your position.

1010 Murals reward location

After taking a photo of all five murals, you’ll receive a message from 1010 congratulating you for your efforts. 1010 also sends a photo of the next location, but barely any other info.

In any case, make your way to the southwestern part of Tequesta. There, you’ll see a garage with a keypad. The passcode is--you guessed it--the moniker of the person you’ve been talking to the whole time. Enter 1-0-1-0 to open the shutter door.

Inside, complete with its own cutscene, is the ‘95 Grotti Cheetah. Oh, and this particular garage becomes yours, too, giving you one more slot for a registered car. That does it for our guide on where to find all 1010 Murals in Grand Theft Auto 6. If you’re still searching for other activities that reward awesome cars, we suggest tackling the NoFlushers mission, which leads to the mind-blowing speed demon known as the Truffade Thrax--i.e. Bugatti Chiron lookalike.

title: Nearly Three Decades And Four Consoles Later, I Finally Beat Ocarina Of Time
summary:
I finally did it.

As Princess Zelda held the transformed, monstrous Ganon in place with her magic, I delivered the final blow with the Master Sword. The Demon King was sealed away and Hyrule was saved. I found myself getting emotional, because this was the first time in 28 years that I had beaten The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. 

For many, that would mean it was also the first time they had played Ocarina of Time, but this wasn't the case for me. I first played the game, if you can call running around Kokiri Forest "playing the game," back around launch in 1998, when I was four years old. It was my older brother's Nintendo 64, and his copy of the game, which he had already completed. My adventures in Hyrule primarily consisted of exploring Hyrule Field and switching between the child and adult timelines. I even loved flipping through my brother's strategy guide to the point that my mom got it spiral bound at Kinko's. 

But I never made any progress. The animation of Link pulling the Master Sword from its marble resting place was mesmerizing to me, but to be completely honest … Ganondorf terrified me too much to want to actually face him in the climactic battle. I distinctly remember a moment at summer camp a short time later, when each camper was asked to share a fear. Some were afraid of snakes. Some picked spiders or the dark. I said "Ganondorf" without a second thought, and I meant it. He was terrifying! His evil smirk when looking down on Link as he chased Zelda and Impa out of the castle was burned into my brain. 

I started and ultimately fizzled out on a few more playthroughs on Nintendo 64, and eventually picked up a new version of Ocarina of Time for GameCube a few years later--the Legend of Zelda: Collector's Edition, which was pretty much the same experience but with a better controller. Still, I found myself struggling to get any further, and I put the game aside in favor of Super Smash Bros. I sure wish I hadn't opened it, too, considering how ridiculously valuable it is today. 

It would be many years before I made another attempt, this time on 3DS. This version was marketed as a big improvement over the original Nintendo 64 release, and it's hard to deny that, even from the game's early moments. The motion controls on 3DS made aiming the slingshot remarkably easy, and the much-needed visual overhaul made the characters seem more like people. But still, despite loving what I played, I drifted away. This time, it was shortly after finishing the Forest Temple, and though I planned to go back and finish the rest of the game, that never happened. 

As the years passed, I had resigned myself to the fact, or what I thought was a fact, that I would never finish Ocarina of Time. I still had a great appreciation for what it brought to the medium, but I wasn't champing at the bit to give it another try. 

That was, of course, until Nintendo decided to remake the game again, this time on Nintendo Switch 2. Caught up in the excitement of so many of my friends and colleagues playing Ocarina of Time again, I decided to give it another shot--and to be completely honest, I wasn't sure things would be any different this time. 

Maybe it was everyone around me getting caught up in the excitement of playing Ocarina of Time together. Maybe it was being able to sing the songs instead of having to press the buttons. It might have just been that the game had less friction this time, with the motion-controlled aiming and movable camera just making it more enjoyable to play. 

It was likely some combination of all of these factors that kept me hooked past when I would usually burn out and move on to a different game. After making it past the Forest Temple, Fire Temple, and Water Temple, it occurred to me that I was actually nearing the final battle with Ganondorf. A few hours later, I had all the Sages on board, and I made my way into Ganondorf's imposing tower.

Just from absorbing gaming pop-culture over the years, I knew to expect his aggressive organ music as I climbed to the top, but it still felt monumental. Frankly, I even already knew the strategy for beating him, but finally getting to do it myself--and then deliver the "real" final blow against his monstrous Ganon form--was like finally closing a chapter in my life. Ocarina of Time was one of the first video games I can remember watching someone play, and I probably would never have finally seen the credits roll if this remake didn't exist. 

Thanks, Nintendo.

title: Rockstar Games Has A GTA 6 Hit On Its Hands, But Its Union Vote Is A Loss
summary:
Roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB). The news came in the wake of GTA 6's record-breaking launch, and had the IWGB been recognized, Rockstar Games management would have been legally obligated to negotiate collective bargaining terms with the union on topics such as pay, hours, and conditions.

Voting took place across two weeks, and turnout was massive, with over 93% of UK staff casting their ballot (roughly 1,544 employees). The IWGB said it was undeterred by the result and would continue working to build support among Rockstar employees. "While the result means Rockstar will not be formally required to hold regular meetings with union representatives under a recognition agreement, it does not prevent workers from continuing to organize and push for workplace improvements through the IWGB, joining the union or exercising their individual trade union rights and protections," the union said in a statement.

The vote also comes hot on the heels of the IWGB taking Rockstar to an employment tribunal, alleging unlawful dismissal and union busting after it fired over 30 employees last year for gross misconduct over alleged leaks of confidential information. Closing submissions were wrapped up shortly before the vote results came out, and a ruling is still pending. While game dev unionizing has gained significant momentum over the years, a decisive loss at one of the industry's biggest studios could be a notable speed bump for union organizers.

With Rockstar also riding the wave of GTA 6's monumental success, employees may be focused on bonuses and post-launch momentum, which could make pushing through a formal union structure even harder. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society--this isn't a sign to retreat; it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues,' the IWGB added.

The vote also comes hot on the heels of the IWGB taking Rockstar to an employment tribunal, alleging unlawful dismissal and union busting after it fired over 30 employees last year for gross misconduct over alleged leaks of confidential information. Closing submissions were wrapped up shortly before the vote results came out, and a ruling is still pending. While game dev unionizing has gained significant momentum over the years, a decisive loss at one of the industry's biggest studios could be a notable speed bump for union organizers.

With Rockstar also riding the wave of GTA 6's monumental success, employees may be focused on bonuses and post-launch momentum, which could make pushing through a formal union structure even harder. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society--this isn't a sign to retreat; it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues,' the IWGB added.

title: How To Get The Anime Car In GTA 6
summary:
There are a few ways to get an anime car in GTA 6, but if you don't want to spend any money, we've stumbled upon one just there for the taking. There's no huge mission or shootout to survive; in fact the car owner is randomly rolled when you enter the house. Ours belongs to a guy partaking in some extracurricular activities via the medium of VR. Sure enough, he's pretty distracted, so this one's an easy grab. We've also heard of blindfolded men tied to the bed, and other spicy scenarios.

You'll want to head to Ambrosia, although we've heard of the car spawning in other locations around Key Lento, too. The house in question is right across the road from a garage.

The car is in the garage, and you can just walk in and take it. While this particular anime livery is exclusive to the Declasse Akane, you can take some cars to Tuners mod shops, since they specialize in JDM vehicles, or Vice Auto Customs, where some anime liveries are available to apply to your car.

Be careful taking this car anywhere for work though--don't touch the customization menu or the wrap might be overwritten, and there's no way of getting it back.

If you're wondering which of the hundreds of random activities to attempt next, or maybe you're looking for a specific weapon, check out our GTA 6 guides hub.
